description: We make a wood-plastic composite siding board. Builders want to use it on walls close to the property line on small apartment buildings, where the code calls for noncombustible cladding. We have cone calorimeter results and a flame-spread rating of 75 but we have not done the full-scale exterior wall fire test. What do we need to get it accepted in Alberta?
known_facts: intended where noncombustible cladding is required
cone calorimeter data and flame-spread rating 75

missing_info.field: intended building height, building area and dwelling arrangement
missing_info.why: Small apartment buildings alone does not establish Part 9 versus Part 3 applicability.

missing_info.field: limiting distance and maximum permitted unprotected-opening percentage
missing_info.why: The construction table and the tested-wall permission have different conditions.

missing_info.field: complete wall construction and applicable tested or prescriptive assembly route
missing_info.why: A missing full-scale test does not by itself prove that all acceptable-solution routes fail.

missing_info.field: specific building, limiting distance and opening percentage
missing_info.why: the required construction depends on the exposing building face

should_cite.why: Candidate benchmark only; deciding facts must be obtained first.
Candidate tested-wall cladding permission, conditional on maximum permitted opening percentage and other stated limits.
full-scale test acceptance criteria referenced by the Part 9 route

gold.engineering_reason: Depends on the building it goes on: buildings outside the Division C exemption need registered professionals.

identify_gold_candidates.label: model-checked, not human-verified
identify_gold_candidates.quote: each exposing building face and any exterior wall located above an exposing building face that encloses an attic or roof space shall be constructed in conformance with Table 9.10.14.5.-A
identify_gold_candidates.reasoning: The applicant says the code 'calls for noncombustible cladding' on walls close to the property line of small apartment buildings; in Part 9 that cladding requirement comes from Table 9.10.14.5.-A via Sentence (1). 9.10.14. (not 9.10.15.) is the Part 9 subsection for apartment buildings unless no dwelling unit is above another (9.10.15.1.(1)), which the description doesn't say.

identify_gold_candidates.label: model-checked, not human-verified
identify_gold_candidates.quote: need not be noncombustible where the wall assembly complies with the requirements of Clause 3.1.5.5.(1)(b) when tested in conformance with CAN/ULC-S134
identify_gold_candidates.reasoning: The full-scale test the manufacturer hasn't done is the tested-wall permission; useful to rank, but it is the route not taken, not the provision varied.

identify_gold_candidates.label: model-checked, not human-verified
identify_gold_candidates.quote: the fire-resistance rating, construction and cladding for exposing building faces of buildings or fire compartments of Group A, B, C, D or Group F, Division 3 occupancy classification shall comply with Table 3.2.3.7.
identify_gold_candidates.reasoning: Part 3 branch: if the 'small apartment buildings' exceed Part 9 limits (height/area not given), the same cladding requirement comes from 3.2.3.7.(1).
